title: Slack Twilio Integration: How to Set It Up (2026)
summary: A Slack Twilio integration connects your chat to SMS messages. You can set this up in under an hour without writing any code.
body_markdown:
## Building One Slack Twilio Workflow Step by Step


When your tool lacks a step, an HTTP request to a documented endpoint fills it. The first flow is one Slack message in and one text message out, built in four steps.


Read the list below before you start, because it gives the build in order and each step leaves one working integration behind it.


1. Create the workflow. An empty flow exists, and nothing runs yet.
2. Connect Slack. The tool can now read the channel you chose.
3. Add the trigger. A new message in that channel starts a run.
4. Connect Twilio. The tool can now send from your Twilio number.
5. Map the fields. The Slack message text becomes the body of the text message.
6. Add a filter. Only messages that match your rule continue to the send step.
7. Test. One real message runs through, and a text arrives on your phone.
8. Publish. The flow runs on every matching message without you.


Taking these steps in pairs, the four stages below start with the empty workflow.


Name the workflow for what it does, such as "Urgent Slack alert to SMS", so it's findable once a second flow exists. Pick the Slack trigger for a new message in a channel and point it at one channel only.


Scoping the trigger to a single channel keeps early runs predictable, and that matters because the first team to put a busy channel on a trigger will text everyone on the roster by accident.


### Stage 2: Connect Slack and Twilio


When you connect each app, a dialog asks for authorization. In Slack, approve access to the workspace and the channel. In Twilio, paste your account credentials and choose the number you send from.


Keep each connection as its own saved entry rather than re-entering credentials per workflow.


A saved connection is the cheapest template you have, because every later flow starts with both apps already authorized, and that's the lever that makes the second build faster than the first.


You don't hire for this, you describe it: in Activepieces, tell the built-in chat you want a new message in one Slack channel sent on as a Twilio text, and it builds and publishes the flow.


That flow is the same artifact you would have assembled by hand in the steps above, and it sits under the same RBAC and audit logs as every flow a person built, with every run leaving a trace anyone on the team can read without special training.


MoneyGram and Moneypenny run Activepieces in production, and you can test the claim by describing your alert in the chat and opening the live flow and run trace it leaves in your account.


### Mapping Slack fields to Twilio and testing


Map the Slack message text to the body of the Twilio message, and type the recipient number into the destination field. Then add a filter ahead of the send step so that only messages containing your chosen keyword continue.


Without it, every casual message becomes a text.


If your tool has no Twilio send action, an HTTP request to Twilio's messages endpoint carries the same three fields: destination, sender and body.


Post a matching message in the channel, run the test, and confirm the text reaches your phone. A pass means the trigger, mapping and filter all work together. A failure points to one step, because the test output shows where the run stopped.


Publish, then post one more matching message and one that should be filtered out.


The first should arrive as a text and the second should show as a stopped run in the run history. Seeing both outcomes confirms the filter is doing its job in production, not only in the test.
